name: Adam Valkin
description: I grew up in Johannesburg, South Africa, and made my way to the U.S. thanks to college tennis and curiosity. At Harvard, I studied Economics and History, and through a chance introduction, I landed my first job at an internet startup. That experience sparked a career full of adventure across tech, entrepreneurship, and investing – with chapters in London, New York, and Boston. I have spent two decades in venture capital, with the Hoegh family, Accel London, and General Catalyst. I’ve been fortunate to work with many exceptional founders and investors, and I’ve learned just as much from mentoring as I have from being mentored. I don’t take that for granted; it keeps me grounded and always learning. I’ve led early and growth-stage investments in Rapyd, Monzo, Melio Payments, Ro Health, Fiverr, Flywire, ClassPass, Superplay, GoCardless, Shift Technology, Finom, Spinny, Array, and others. I’ve also co-led or supported investments in Spotify, Lemonade, Blank Street, and Empathy. Along the way, I’ve incubated a few ventures too—including LOVEFiLM (acquired by Amazon), Propertyfinder (acquired by News Corp), and, most recently, Moment Holdings, a fast-growing payments company in Africa. These days, I split my time between Boston, New York, and Tel Aviv. I’m especially drawn to product-oriented founders who are passionate about shaping the future. I’m focused on early-stage AI apps that tackle familiar verticals, such as financial services, insurance, commerce, media, and healthcare.

name: Alex Moskowitz
description: I’ve never been good at separating the professional from the personal. For me, pursuit of professional excellence, becoming the best you can be at your craft, has always been a means for achieving personal growth. On a human level, I am a deep believer in the concept that you are a product of those you surround yourself with. It is then no surprise that I found in Vine Ventures the same ethos and values that I look for in personal friendships and life partners. Vine is a team who prefers to let our actions speak louder than our words. We care more about passing on opportunities in the right way than winning deals in the wrong way. We intend to keep our partnership small, knowing that we make our best decisions when we can be completely raw and vulnerable with our thoughts, and that requires complete trust. I’m the fourth investment hire the team has made in five years, and my path to Vine was non-linear. I grew up as the oldest of four siblings in Colorado, where technology entrepreneurship was an elusive concept to grasp. You have DISH Network, which famously never raised venture dollars, and then you have the likes of Vail Resorts, which I’m sure was considered some sort of startup at some point. There were of course others, but the point is, it wasn’t Silicon Valley. So I set out to learn: I moved to California to attend UC Berkeley and began gathering experiences that would help me understand how generational, enduring companies are built. I started my career as an investment banker with Moelis & Company and as a private equity investor with Lindsay Goldberg. Both firms had swanky offices in the middle of midtown Manhattan, and both experiences left me with a deep feeling of wanting something more inspiring out of life. The jobs were stimulating, don’t get me wrong, and I was objectively lucky to be there by all measures. But it wasn’t fulfilling on a personal level. I left to learn how you actually build companies instead of sitting in an ivory tower pretending to do so. I was fortunate to find great mentors in Marcela and Jess who were building Alfred, a software & tech-enabled residential management platform backed by NEA and Spark. It was a three year journey of the highest highs and lowest lows, one that gave me a deep appreciation for what it takes to build a generational company. After raising $150M in capital, launching new products, acquiring strategic assets, and helping to pivot the business to 4x growth in revenue, I decided to help many more founders through that same journey as a VC. I was fortunate to find OpenView as my first home in venture, a firm notorious for rigor in underwriting and creativity in firm building. OpenView had spent 18 years pushing the boundaries for how traditional venture firms service founders, and I take those learnings with me to Vine. When not working, I find joy in supporting my new wife and my three siblings on their personal and professional endeavors. You can find us chatting about the latest SciFi books/TV shows while snowboarding, at a concert, or at home with an ever growing list of feline/canine friends.

name: Barak Kaufman
description: I started my career cold-calling founders, “selling money”, on the investment team at Insight Partners with Eric Reiner. I subsequently left to start my own company, Intello (“SaaS to manage SaaS”). I made a ton of mistakes yet listened enough to find the need customers had with SaaS security, culminating in a successful exit to SailPoint in 2021. After the acquisition, I took some time to recharge while vesting & resting at SailPoint, incubating two health tech businesses on the side and running a few founder communities, including one for post-exit founders. I’m also an active angel investor. Most of my time is spent helping founders at the pre-idea and idea stage. Specifically, with post-exit founders who are navigating the “what’s next” questions. I love the 0 to 1 stage and plan to partner with epic founders building missionary companies for the rest of my career.

name: Dan Povitsky
description: Vine Ventures is the closest it gets to partnering with a VC that understands the founder mentality. We did not inherit a portfolio, an office, or investors; rather, we built our firm from the ground-up to deliver a world-class experience to founders, employees, and limited partners. Today, we are one of the largest seed-focused firms in NYC with a differentiated footprint in Tel Aviv and San Francisco. With the goal of being the go-to funding source for early-stage entrepreneurs in our target markets, I’ve relocated to each as we set up our operations on the West Coast and in Israel. I happily go where our team needs me most and am involved across significant parts of our portfolio, supporting founders in strategy, hiring, fundraising, and most importantly: balancing listening and speaking, always with a solutions-oriented approach. I started my career at Credit Suisse (in 2013, when the TMT group took Alibaba public) and TA Associates (investing and running global M&A for a portfolio roll-up). With an entrepreneurial itch, in 2018, I was fortunate to find in Eric Reiner a partner I aligned with morally, ethically, and in our mutual pursuit of becoming the best at our craft. Through a single family office-backed fund, we invested early in a handful of companies that became standouts of their vintage: Carta, Hippo, Roman, Unqork, and Front. That track-record and the support of founders and mentors allowed us to go institutional and launch Vine. Today, we support a diverse portfolio of entrepreneurs as their lead investors; and I’m proud to say we have helped them achieve a range of personal and professional milestones, including one of the highest graduation rates (from Seed to Series A and B) in the industry. I’m a big believer in focusing on your power-skill, embracing what makes you different, and developing your unique advantage to win. Test-taking not being my strength, as a teenager I focused on cross country and track to improve my chances in college admissions. Hard work (and coaches’ belief) became my ticket to the University of Chicago where I was lucky to earn enduring friendships, a couple conference titles, and a degree in Economics. To this day, I get the most enjoyment from team accomplishments and am grateful to work with founders and LPs alongside one of the best early stage investing teams in venture. When not working, I devote time to family and close friends, with whom I hope to be more often hiking, skiing, and adventuring.

name: Demren Sinik
description: The first sentence of a VC bio is supposed to be inspiring. Thankfully, I prefer to focus on second impressions. I grew up in Los Angeles and received my undergraduate degree from Harvard, where I was determined to study subjects that had no application to the real world. I majored in theoretical math because I obsess over logic riddles and minored in English because I obsess over Vladimir Nabokov. Little did I know these passions would manifest in surprising ways as a VC – whether in reading research papers, writing yet another blog post, or connecting on a deeper level with founders. After graduating, I moved to New York City and spent over three years at Blackstone Private Equity. Focusing on technology and business services sectors, I was privileged to partner with companies like Ultimate Software, Kronos, Vivint, Cloverleaf, and Gates. Having exposure early in my career to mature, public technology businesses – as an investor, operator, and BOD observer – has made me a profoundly better (and more empathetic) early-stage investor. I joined Vine as the first hire and now lead our efforts on the West Coast and LatAm. I’m a generalist but tend to index towards industries utilizing cutting edge technologies such as machine learning, data, security, and developer tools. Second impressions matter most because venture investing isn’t about the sales pitch on day one. It’s about showing up on day two – fielding your late night calls, finding your next 10x engineer, introducing you to a pipeline of eager enterprise customers. That’s the kind of partner I aspire to be at Vine. Anyone can write a check, but not everyone can invest. Backing the next cohort of generational technology companies is busy work. But in my limited free time, you can find me at the nearest cinema or taking extremely high risk bets on my skis.

name: Eric Reiner
description: Vine Ventures is an inseparable part of who I am. It is the embodiment of what I hope to accomplish with the “work” part of my time on this incredible planet. It is a family of like-minded individuals, looking to make money for incredible individuals and institutions, by backing some of the most heroic, brave, and determined creators in the world. We started Vine in 2020, receiving our first Limited Partner commitments days before COVID-19 broke out. Vine is a resilient founding team just like the ones we back; dedicated to innovating and developing the best user experience for founders beginning their process of creation. Before forming the team and capital behind Vine, I was with Insight Venture Partners, where I spent my days relentlessly searching for founders of growth-stage companies, and made investments in several including Xamarin (acquired by MSFT) and 1stdibs (DIBS – NASDAQ). Following Insight, I joined my friend Liad Agmon at Dynamic Yield to help build out the US presence of the Israeli software company that would ultimately get acquired by McDonald’s for a reported $300m. Immediately before Vine, I co-founded a venture capital firm called Sinai Ventures, backed by a single family office of one of the founders of SAP, where I was fortunate to lead early investments in companies like Carta, Hippo, Ro, Unqork, FrontApp, Ramp, Dutchie, and others. Vine is the outcome of a career and dream to combine our team’s experience and track record to build a new generation of venture capital firms. We are your peers, not your parents, and our LP base and operator network of some of the most powerful people in industry and finance can fundamentally impact the trajectory of your company. I am a grateful husband to Arianne and father to Sophie and Salo. I enjoy playing racquet sports and am uniquely available as a wedding DJ, Photographer, and Rabbi. I am a board member of United Hatzalah.

name: Idan Tendler
description: I’m a repeat cybersecurity founder and operator. Most recently, I served as SVP and led the Application Security business at Palo Alto Networks after they acquired Bridgecrew, a company I co-founded and led to bring developer-first security to the cloud. Before that, I led and co-founded Fortscale, one of the earliest players in user behavior analytics, which was acquired by RSA Security. I got my start building the cybersecurity business unit at Elbit Systems and served as a commander in 8200, where I first learned how to innovate and lead under pressure and scale technical teams with purpose. Over the years, I’ve grown increasingly committed to building not just companies, but non profit organizations. I founded and serve as Chairman of Anu Banu , an organization that mobilizes the Israeli tech sector toward social activism and impact, It incubated variety of initiatives including – Place-IL to open doors into tech for underrepresented talent across Israel; the Israeli Tech Negev Fund to create hundreds of quality jobs in the country’s south; or Ir Medina , to bridge between Israel’s high‑tech ecosystem and local municipalities in the periphery. These initiatives aren’t side projects, they shape how I show up as a partner to founders. I care deeply about how companies affect the world around them. I’ve seen firsthand how tech can be a force multiplier for inclusion, resilience, and long-term national strength. The Israeli ecosystem has given me so much; my work now is about helping extend that opportunity to more people and places, while backing the next generation of founders building with the same kind of purpose and excellence.

name: John McIlree
description: I joined Vine after nearly a decade at GCM Grosvenor, a multi-billion dollar institutional investment allocator. At GCM, I spent time in roles ranging from business analyst to accountant to a member of the deal team. Most recently, I was a Principal in Operational Due Diligence, where I was responsible for detailed evaluation of fund managers, including emerging managers and venture capital funds. It was my time on the ODD team where I was exposed to VC managers’ internal operations; and where I developed my interest in how to design these operations to mitigate non-investment risk. In other words, what it takes to build an institutional-quality firm. Building and understanding how things work is my inner compass. I studied Mechanical Engineering at Northwestern University, where friends and I designed and built CAD models, robots, and even a capacitance-sensing musical instrument. Today, I spend less time on building physical things and more time on building Vine with the team. While Vine’s investors take a detailed and diligent approach to backing founders, I mirror that mindset in managing Vine’s operations. By marrying process with reality, I reduce any friction to delivering on our objectives for our founders, employees, and limited partners. I live in Chicago with my wife and son, who was born on Open Championship Sunday in 2022 and has already visited the Vine offices in Tel Aviv! I love golf, am a diehard Denver Broncos fan, and am looking forward to rebuilding one of my old sets of golf clubs to fit my son when the time arrives.

Advance replaces that patchwork with purpose-built banking infrastructure, giving insurance businesses the speed, transparency, and control they need to manage their finances with confidence. Advance was founded in 2024 by Omer Rimoch (CEO) and Gal Dreiman (CTO) and is Based in New York.

It requires integrated execution across marketing, data, and capital, which product innovators and DTC brands simply don’t have access to. Until now. The ZyG platform validates scale potential before launch, executes every stage of the customer lifecycle, and removes much of the financing risk involved in scaling a DTC brand. description: Tenna Systems (formerly Tip & Cue Inc.) is a software-first spectrum intelligence company building the world’s first dynamic, unified map of the electromagnetic spectrum. Tenna was founded by twin brothers Avner and Gabriel Bendheim with decades leading signals intelligence (SIGINT) and electronic warfare programs.

CardinalOps optimizes threat coverage by delivering AI-powered recommendations for widely used security analytics solutions like Splunk, Microsoft Sentinel, IBM QRadar, and CrowdStrike, mapped to MITRE ATT&CK threat models. Our cloud-based platform does the job of skilled detection engineers with years of experience – but faster and without the risk of human error. The company was founded in February 2020 (just as the pandemic broke). Its founders are Michael Mumcuoglu (CEO) and Yair Manor (CTO).

name: planck
description: Planck provides an AI-based data platform for commercial insurance, working with top US insurance companies and helping them increase premiums while reducing loss and expense ratios. Its mission is to empower commercial insurers by generating insights that streamline the commercial underwriting process, enabling insurers to instantly and accurately underwrite any policy. Planck was founded by a team of serial entrepreneurs with an extensive background in insurance and technology.

name: Global Data Center
description: Global Data Center was founded in 2013 by Moshe Lasman in cooperation and with the financial backing of the Viola Group, a leading private equity investment firm. The Company is operating two highly secure, sub-terranean data centers in the area of Tel Aviv, one in Herzliya Pituach, and the second in Petah Tikva. Both sites are built in accordance with the Tier 3 Uptime global standard that serves as the current standard for advanced data centers. The company was acquired by EdgeConneX® , a pioneer in global Hyperlocal to Hyperscale Data Center Solutions, in 2021.

name: TRUEACCORD
description: TrueAccord is the intelligent, digital-first collection and recovery company that leaders across industries trust to drive breakthrough results while delivering a superior consumer experience. TrueAccord pioneered the industry’s only adaptive intelligence: a patented machine learning engine, powered by engagement data from over 16 million consumer journeys, that dynamically personalizes every facet of the consumer experience – from channel to message to plan type and more – in real-time. Combined with code-based compliance and a self-serve digital experience, TrueAccord delivers liquidation and recovery rates 50-80% higher than industry benchmarks. The TrueAccord product suite includes Retain, an early-stage recovery solution, and Recover, a full-service debt collection platform. www.trueaccord.com

name: Oversi
description: Oversi Networks is a leading global provider of OTT rich-media caching and content delivery solutions that help service providers relieve the heavy network congestion associated with P2P and Internet video traffic. Acquired by Allot Communications (NASDAQ: ALLT).

name: Candivore
description: Founded in 2018, Candivore is a leading, independent mobile gaming studio based in Tel Aviv, Israel. Its hit game Match Masters has been downloaded more than 50 million times. Candivore employs 70 highly engaged team members that share a passion for creating amazing game experiences for their players. Prior investors in Candivore include vgames, Union Tech Ventures and O.G. Tech Venture Partners. For more information, please visit www.candivore.io .

name: Pliops
description: Pliops is developing a new NAND storage processor technology enabling the next generation of cloud and data center applications. Their disruptive technology significantly simplifies the storage stack thus enabling highly scalable storage and DB solutions with optimal cost, power consumption and performance improvements. Founded in 2017 by flash storage industry veterans Uri Beitler (CEO), Moshe Twitto (CTO) & Aryeh Mergi (Chairman).

name: Cowbell Cyber
description: At Cowbell Cyber, we provide standalone, individualized, and easy-to-understand cyber insurance to small and medium-sized enterprises. Our AI-assisted, continuous underwriting process enables brokers to issue coverage in minutes. Our policies, bundled with risk monitoring and incident preparedness and response resources, deliver value to policyholders on day-one.

name: Insurify
description: At Insurify , we’re reimagining the way you compare, buy, and manage your insurance online. By harnessing the power of artificial intelligence, we make insurance shopping simple, affordable, and hassle-free. When it comes to making your life easier, we make no compromises. Year Founded: 2013 Snejina Zacharia, MBA (MIT), Founder & CEO Giorgos Zacharia, PhD (MIT), Co-founder & Board Member Tod Kiryazov, MBA (Northeastern), Co-founder & CPO

name: Origami Logic
description: Origami Logic is a marketing analytics company that helps teams master marketing performance by letting them see what’s working and what’s not – in a way that makes sense to them – so they can optimize their efforts. Thousands of marketers and global brands, including P&G, AB InBev, Diageo and Kellogg’s, trust Origami Logic to help them unify and refine their vast array of marketing data, across every channel and platform, so they can search and organize it in real time to get a better understanding of their marketing efforts and improve their overall impact.

name: MDClone
description: MDClone offers an innovative, self-service data analytics environment powering exploration, discovery, and collaboration throughout the healthcare ecosystems, cross-institutionally, and globally. The powerful underlying infrastructure of the MDClone ADAMS Platform allows users to overcome common barriers in healthcare in order to organize, access and protect the privacy of patient data while accelerating research, improving operations and quality, and driving innovation to deliver better patient outcomes. Founded in Israel in 2016, MDClone serves major health systems, payers, and life science customers in the United States, Canada, and Israel.

name: EX.CO
description: EX.CO is the smarter video technology harnessing the power of machine learning to maximize revenue across every screen: web, mobile, CTV, and DOOH. As a trusted partner to media leaders worldwide—including Advance Local, Hearst Newspapers, Motorsport Network, The Arena Group, and Ziff Davis—EX.CO sets the standard for video monetization with its online video platform and AI-driven yield engine, built for growth, control, and transparency. EX.CO has been shaping the future of video since 2012. Headquartered in New York City with a global team, we are proudly backed by The Walt Disney Company, Saban Ventures, Viola Group, 83North, and others. Learn more at ex.co. The company is managed by Tom Pachys (co-founder, CEO) and Shachar Orren (co-founder, CRO/CMO).

name: Speedata
description: Speedata has developed the world’s first dedicated accelerated processor unit (APU) for big data analytics across industries. Speedata’s processor was designed to optimize datacenter and cloud-based database and analytic workloads, dramatically improving performance by orders of magnitude while reducing costs, power consumption and space. The company was founded by a multidisciplinary team of seasoned semiconductor veterans with innovative academic experts.

name: Trigo
description: Trigo powers grocery stores with market leading frictionless checkout and digitized operations. AI-driven and fully automated, Trigo’s proven solution layers digital commerce capabilities onto existing store spaces. Trigo-powered stores enable retailers to reduce costs, base business decisions on an unbiased view of what's happening in-store, improve customer experience, cultivate nimble logistics, and open up new pathways to profitable growth. The company was founded in 2018 by Michael Gabay (CEO) and Daniel Gabay (CTO) and has more than 120 employees. Trigo’s offices are home to a diverse group of professionals in Israel, USA, Germany, UK and more.

name: restless
description: Rest Less is the UK’s largest and fastest growing jobs, advice and community site for the over-50s. Since launching in late 2018, we have seen rapid growth and have quickly established ourselves as the leading authority in the over-50s jobs and career advice space. Rest Less supports its members through what can be a huge transitional point in life - a time that can be hugely exciting, but also daunting and challenging for some. With life expectancy continuing to rise, and almost all population growth coming from the over-50s – we want to help our members grasp the opportunity that this time in their life presents. The company was founded in 2018 by Stuart Lewis and Sara Stephens.

name: Lin health
description: Lin is a digital health company with the vision of driving better outcomes for people with chronic primary pain. The Lin team is building the first truly digital pain care clinic that will manage patients and connect them to a remote care system. Lin is addressing the massive unmet need in the treatment of chronic pain. Prevalence of chronic pain in the western world is increasing rapidly and traditional healthcare systems are not properly equipped to manage and treat these patients. There is a significant shortage in pain specialists and traditional therapeutic options are addictive and harmful. Lin Health will address this unmet need by leveraging telehealth solutions and non-opioid treatments to give these patients the comprehensive care they need.

name: Grover
description: Grover offers an on-demand subscription alternative to gadget ownership. The company provides consumers and businesses with the option to access a variety of tech products on a monthly rental basis with the advantage that they can switch or upgrade at any time, depending on their individual needs and budget. Grover is an advocate of the Circular Economy, contributing to the reduction of technology underutilization and e-waste through product recirculation. Founded in 2015 by Michael Cassau

investors: Mirae Asset-LG Electronics New Growth Fund

name: HyperGuest
description: HyperGuest is the B2B marketplace for the hospitality industry. Our technology enables superb profitability and user experience, by removing all barriers between supply and demand in this highly fragmented industry landscape. HyperGuest enables direct booking transactions between hotels and travel service providers. Accomodation rooms and rates are shared through an electronic marketplace that assures rate transparency, content accuracy, payment confidence, transaction success and higher margins.

name: Rapid
description: RapidAPI is the world's largest API Marketplace where millions of developers can find, test, and connect to thousands of APIs - all with a single account, API key, and SDK. Software developers can also share and collaborate on internal APIs using RapidAPI for Teams , a common workspace to publish internal APIs, and share public API subscriptions. In turn, organizations can use RapidAPI Enterprise Hub to create a centralized hub environment to help developers reuse and connect to existing APIs faster while providing IT with enterprise-wide visibility and governance of API consumption. Founder: Iddo Gino, CEO

name: Omnius
description: Founded in 2015, omni:us provides its customers with AI-based claims management solutions that enable insurers to rapidly deploy artificial intelligence in their various business lines. The modular approach of these solutions supports multiple use cases, enabling a smooth user experience during a claim, while measurably increasing customer satisfaction, optimizing costs and reducing leakage. The omni:us suite offers the flexibility to customize and adapt to insurers' existing legacy or state-of-the-art systems.

name: VGames
description: vgames is the venture fund for game entrepreneurs. Having both worked with some of the youngest and most mature developers, they have a deep understanding of what it takes to build a great game. They are passionate about games, and about supporting companies as they grow to become global leaders.

name: Summer
description: Summer is on a mission to provide more people with access to vacation homes by eliminating the headache and risk associated with purchase

name: Juganu
description: Juganu transforms existing lighting infrastructure into an AI-powered edge platform for cities, local governments, campuses, and large public venues. By replacing standard lights with connected smart fixtures, Juganu enables high-resolution video, Wi-Fi, real-time alerts, video analytics, and lighting management without trenching, cabling, or long deployment cycles. The platform helps cities and public-space operators improve safety, mobility, connectivity, energy efficiency, and situational awareness through a unified infrastructure layer. Juganu is deployed across multiple U.S. cities and venues, supporting smart city, stadium, mobility, public-space, and selected indoor and retail use cases.

name: Taranis
description: Taranis is a leading precision agriculture intelligence platform that uses sophisticated computer vision, data science and deep learning algorithms to effectively monitor fields. The system enables farmers to make informed decisions by detecting early symptoms of weeds, uneven emergence, nutrient deficiencies, disease or insect infestations, water damage and equipment problems. Overseeing millions of acres of farmland in Argentina, Brazil, Russia, Ukraine and the United States, Taranis gives farmers the tools to address issues in real time, increasing yields and cutting costs. Founded in 2014, Taranis employs over 45 people worldwide and is headquartered in Tel Aviv with subsidiaries in Argentina, Brazil and the US. Pictured (left to right): Amihay Gornik (VP Aeronautics), Ofir Schlam (Co-founder & CEO), Ayal Karmi (Co-founder & COO), Eli Bukchin (Co-founder & CTO) & Asaf Horvitz (Co-founder & VP Architect).

name: Candis
description: CANDIS was founded in 2015 by Christopher Becker and Christian Ritosek with the goal to automate manual bookkeeping processes with intelligent software. Eliminating manual data entry and reconciliation, bookkeeping and accounting departments of companies become up to 5 times more efficient.

name: Inshur
description: INSHUR is the only fully digital insurance platform for today’s commercial and ride-share drivers, owners, and fleets, and is the fastest growing provider of auto insurance for TLC (New York) and Private Hire drivers (UK). The company's mobile app allows drivers to quote, purchase and service an insurance policy at their convenience via their mobile. INSHUR eliminates the need to call or visit brokers, wait for a quote, find parking, mail payments and deal with missing paperwork. Owner-operator drivers for black car bases like Uber, Lyft, Gett and others enjoy benefits like exclusive insurance rates and coverage comparisons, a policy using a credit/debit card with no fees, and a range of tasks that can all be done via the app, like managing documents, reporting claims, and making policy changes - all while receiving real-time alerts for items that require attention The company was founded in October 2016 by Dan Bratshpis (CEO) and David Daiches (COO), and is based in New York and Brighton (UK).

name: Rewire
description: Rewire is building the first international banking platform for migrants, providing a complete solution to their global financial needs in both their country of residence and country of origin. Rewire's holistic solution is based on a unique and innovative platform that provides customers with a dual cross-border account: One which is remote, for everyday life in their country of residence, and one in their country of origin. This allows them to seamlessly switch between the two accounts with the flick of a button and manage all their financial needs, including depositing their salary, getting a debit card, sending their money back home and even applying for a loan. Rewire was founded in 2015 by (pictured from left to right): Adi Ben-Dayan (VP R&D), Saar Yahalom (CTO), Guy Kashtan (CEO) and Or Ben-Oz.

name: Applicaster
description: Applicaster is a leading video solutions provider for broadcasting, media, and sports. Our no-code SaaS platform for app development combines control, flexibility, and efficiency to drive business performance. A trusted partner of choice for a growing number of video solution providers, Applicaster is an approved Apple, Roku, and Comcast Technology Solutions partner. www.applicaster.com

name: Cellwize
description: Cellwize is all about enabling the networks of the future, today. With Chime, their cloudified and AI-driven RAN automation and orchestration platform, they enable mobile network operators (MNOs) to accelerate 5G network deployment and go-to-market, as well as the ROI on their network investments. Even in the most complex and dynamic of network environments, Chime enables operators to connect to any application and any vendor, as well as co-create on top of the platform, delivering unprecedented ease, speed, and agility. With the future of 5G already here, Chime is helping leading MNOs all over the world to launch and leverage their next generation networks and face the future with confidence. CEO : Ofir Zemer Cellwize was acquired by Qualcomm on June 2022

name: Spott
description: Spott is a data-powered insurtech platform built for eCommerce. To fortify eCommerce businesses against lawsuits, sales disruptions, and unexpected financial losses, Spott created a new breed of dynamic insurance products, including Liability Insurance, Suspension Coverage, and Stockout Protection. All products leverage Spott’s real-time risk data platform to enable continuous, high-resolution observations of the eCommerce business’ digital footprint to assess and price risk accurately. Spott makes merchants resilient by offering them one-click coverage at the best price. The company was acquired by Payoneer in 2022.

name: Dynamic Yield
description: Dynamic Yield ’s personalization technology stack helps marketers increase revenue by automatically personalizing each customer interaction across the web, mobile web, mobile apps and email. The company’s advanced customer segmentation engine uses machine learning to build actionable customer segments in real time, enabling marketers to take instant action via personalization, recommendations, automatic optimization & real-time messaging - in a single platform. Dynamic Yield personalizes the experiences of more than 600 million users globally and counts industry leaders like IKEA, Urban Outfitters, Ocado, and Stitch Fix among its many customers. The company is based in New York and has more than 170 employees in six offices worldwide. Founded in 2011 by (pictured from left to right): Omri Mendellevich (CTO) & Liad Agmon (CEO). The company was acquired by McDonald's (and in 2021 by Mastercard)

name: Tookitaki
description: Tookitaki is innovating the regulatory compliance space by moving beyond rules-based applications and introducing software solutions to maximize efficiency and reduce risks in compliance processes. Their mission is to provide machine learning-powered regulatory compliance solutions that are auditable, scalable and actionable. In the regulatory compliance space, they focus on anti-money laundering and reconciliation management. Incorporated in November 2014 in Singapore , the company is led by a core team with cumulative 150-years’ experience in finance, AI, Big Data Analytics and financial crime. They have offices in Singapore, the US and India. The uniqueness and robustness of their innovation in the field of machine learning have been acknowledged locally and worldwide. They were selected as a Technology Pioneer (2019 cohort) by the World Economic Forum. Other recognitions include SG:D Techblazer Silver Award 2019 (Most Promising Innovation) and MAS Fintech Award 2016 (SME Category).

name: Perfecto
description: Perfecto is the leading cloud-based platform for web, mobile and IoT software testing, empowering global enterprises with the tools they need to deliver better digital experiences for their users. With Perfecto, developers and testers can implement continuous testing throughout the DevOps cycle, using the most reliable lab offering real browsers, smartphones and devices using real-world networks, locations and scenarios. With more than 3,000 customers across all major industries, Perfecto is enabling faster release cycles that set the speed of digital innovation. Founded in 2006 by Eran Yaniv (CEO), Yoram Mizrachi (CTO), Jacky Allal (VP BizDev, deceased) Exit: The company was acquired by Perforce in December 2018.

name: LiveU
description: LiveU is driving the live video revolution, providing live video streaming for TV, mobile, online and social media. LiveU makes it possible for audiences to become part of the story, with high-quality and flawless live video transmitted from anywhere in the world, through the use of patented bonding and video transport technology. LiveU creates a consistent bandwidth and a reliable connection that enables the acquisition, management and distribution of high quality remote live broadcasts over IP. The company’s broad portfolio of products sets the industry standard for live video production. From backpacks to smartphones, and satellite/cellular hybrid to external antenna solutions, LiveU offers a complete range of devices for live video coverage anytime, anywhere. In addition, LiveU offers extensive cloud-based management and video distribution solutions. With over 2,000 customers in 80+ countries, LiveU’s technology is the solution of choice for global broadcasters, online media, news agencies and social media. Founded in 2006 by Samuel (Shmulik) Wasserman (CEO), Avichai (Avi) Cohen (COO) and Dr. Rony Ohayon (CTO).

name: Bluedot
description: Bluedot is a global B2B SaaS company that provides automated VAT recovery and governance solutions to large, multinational companies. Bluedot provides innovative, fully automated, data driven solutions that maximize VAT returns and provide visibility and compliance across all global entities. Founded in 2013 by CEO Isaac Saft (pictured) and President Noam Guzman.

name: Verbit
description: Verbit is a leading voice AI platform trusted by 3,000+ businesses and institutions across legal, education, government, media, and corporate sectors. Verbit delivers transcription, captioning, audio description, dubbing, localization, and translation with unmatched accuracy and scale, powered by its proprietary Captivate™ speech recognition engine and professional human expertise. Purpose-built products like Legal Visor and Legal Capture streamline workflows for law firms and court reporting agencies, while Campus Complete and Civic Complete help educational institutions and government agencies meet ADA Title II compliance. AI-powered dubbing and localization help media reach broader audiences in more languages. Verbit helps organizations improve accessibility, solve compliance needs, and expand their reach.

name: Worthy
description: Worthy is a secure online and secure marketplace for pre-owned luxury goods including diamonds, brand-named watches, jewelry, gemstones and precious metals. The company has developed an unbiased selling platform providing private sellers with the safest and quickest way to auction high-value items to a market of committed buyers and receive the best market value. By making the process simple and conducting guaranteed item grading, Worthy makes it easy for pre-approved buyers to enjoy a steady stream of deals suited to their business needs. Worthy is headquartered in New York City with an R&D facility in Israel.

name: Tapingo
description: Tapingo is a mobile shopping service which allows consumers on-the-go to use their phones to buy food, goods and services directly from physical merchants. Tapingo is focused initially on university campuses. Tapingo presents students with a real-time view of merchant inventories, providing a personalized and efficient shopping and food ordering experience with multiple payment options. Founded in 2012 by Daniel Almog (CEO) and Udi Oster (CTO). Exit: The company was acquired by Grubhub in November 2018.

name: enSilo
description: enSilo protects businesses around the world from data breaches and disruption caused by cyber attacks. The enSilo Endpoint Security Platform comprehensively secures endpoints in real-time pre- and post-infection without alert fatigue, excessive dwell time or breach anxiety while also containing incident response costs by orchestrating automated detection, prevention and incident response actions against advanced malware. enSilo’s patented approach stops advanced malware with a high degree of precision, provides full system visibility and an intuitive user interface and combines next-generation antivirus (NGAV), application communication control, automated endpoint detection and response (EDR) with real-time blocking, threat hunting, incident response, and virtual patching capabilities in a single agent. The platform can be deployed either in the cloud or on-premises and supports multi-tenancy. Founded in 2014 by Roy Katmor (CEO), Udi Yavo (CTO), Tomer Bitton (VP Research) and Ido Kelson (Chief Architect Engineering).

name: Lumenis
description: Lumenis (Nasdaq:LMNS) is a global leader in the field of minimally-invasive clinical solutions for the Surgical, Ophthalmology and Aesthetic markets, and is a world-renowned expert in developing and commercializing innovative energy-based technologies, including Laser, Intense Pulsed Light (IPL) and Radio-Frequency (RF). For nearly 50 years, Lumenis’ ground-breaking products have redefined medical treatments and have set numerous technological and clinical gold-standards. Lumenis has successfully created solutions for previously untreatable conditions, as well as designed advanced technologies that have revolutionized existing treatment methods in each and every one of the verticals we operate in. visit: www.lumenis.com. The company was acquired in 2015 by by XIO Group for approximately $510 million

name: PandoLogic
description: PandoLogic (formerly RealMatch) enables employers to source quality applicants faster and more efficiently through the use of big data, artificial intelligence, and proprietary campaign algorithms that fully-automate and optimize the job advertising process from job classification and targeted distribution to budget allocation and dynamic bidding across diverse job categories. The company's talent acquisition solutions connect publishers, employers, job board operators and job seekers across a shared talent network using the most advanced programmatic platform available. Founded in 2007 by Jonathan Bulkeley (CEO), Motti Mor (Co-founder & COO), Amir Kaldor (CTO) and Avi Balali (VP R&D). Acquired by: Veritone

name: Aeronautics
description: Heading an industry group focused on unmanned solutions, systems and subsystems, Aeronautics Ltd. provides integrated turnkey solutions based on unmanned systems platforms, payloads and communications for defense and civil applications. Designed as leading-edge UAS-based solutions, Aeronautics’ systems offer operationally proven solutions for Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance (ISR) systems requirements. Founded in 1997 by Avi Leumi, Aeronautics has grown to become one of Israel’s largest companies in its domain. Aeronautics’ technology capabilities meet a global growing demand for reliable UAVs and other advanced security systems. Its customer base includes leading governments in developing countries.

name: Gaon Holdings
description: Gaon Holdings , a public company traded on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange, is an operational holdings company that set for itself the goal of leading the development and management of the Israeli water industry, as well as the marketing of water products and projects throughout the world. The Gaon Holdings Group specializes in providing management, control and command solutions for the supply and conveyance of water, gas and fluids to both municipal and industrial bodies, both in Israel and worldwide. The company operates by means of some of the leading industrial companies and factories in Israel. Moreover it is a partner in the capital venture fund Aqua Agro, which invests in startup companies in the fields of water and renewable energies. Gaon Holdings cooperates with leading international companies and is involved in consultations for, and establishment of water purification and treatment plants, management of wastewater recovery, development and control of agricultural projects and more. Founded: 1998 CEO: Guy Regev (pictured)

name: eXelate
description: eXelate , a Nielsen® company, is the leading provider of data technology powering the digital marketing ecosystem. Our customer data cloud™ provides the industry’s only unified customer profiles, which connect identities across all channels and devices - including display, video, audio, offline, mobile and smart TVs - enabling marketers to engage individuals and households with personalized messages to drive performance at scale. eXelate’s data marketplace is the largest 3rd-party cross-device data set in the world with over 5B unique users and devices. eXelate was acquired by Nielsen in March of 2015. Nielsen brings to bear the market’s most powerful proprietary data assets, and together we are not only helping the world’s biggest brands make better and faster marketing and media decisions, we are permanently disrupting the landscape of audience measurement.

name: ParallelM
description: ParallelM provides the fastest and safest path to AI value realization by automating the deployment, orchestration, and management of Machine Learning (ML) in Production, while pioneering the new discipline of ML Ops - Machine Learning Operations Management. Our solutions reduce the time and resources required to deploy and manage ML pipelines in production while at the same time ensuring that they scale and work properly. ParallelM automates the ongoing cycle of operationalization of Machine Learning Applications, while complementing and integrating with existing ML development platforms and analytic engines. Founded by Sivan Metzger (CEO, pictured), Ehud Weinstein (Chairman), Ofir Shalvi (Board Member), Nisha Talagala (CTO), Ofer Bar-Or (COO) and Lior Khermosh (Chief Scientist). Exit: The company was acquired by Datarobot in June 2019

name: orad
description: Orad Hi-Tec Systems is a leading provider of state-of-the-art 3D real-time graphics, video servers, and related workflow management solutions. The Orad product lines allow media organizations and creative professionals more comprehensive workflows with greater choice, flexibility, and operational efficiency The company was acquired in 2015 by Avid (Nasdaq:AVID)

name: Matomy Media Group
description: Matomy Media Group Ltd. (LSE: MTMY, TASE: MTMY.TA) is a global media company with a portfolio of superior data-driven platforms for mobile, video, domain, and email advertising. By providing customized performance and programmatic solutions supported by internal media capabilities, data analytics, and optimization technology, Matomy empowers advertising and media partners to meet their evolving growth-driven goals. Matomy's programmatic platforms include the MobFox SSP, the mobile demand side platform myDSP, and the video advertising platform Optimatic. Founded in 2007 with headquarters in Tel Aviv and 7 offices around the world, Matomy is dual-listed on the London and Tel Aviv Stock Exchanges. CEO: Liam Galin (pictured)

name: Cloudyn
description: Cloudyn monitors and optimizes multi-platform, hybrid cloud deployments to help enterprises fully realize their cloud potential. The SaaS solution delivers visibility into usage, performance and cost, coupled with insights and actionable recommendations for smart optimization and cloud governance. Cloudyn’s solution enables accountability through accurate chargeback and hierarchical cost allocation management. Thousands of global customers rely on Cloudyn, including Fortune 500 leaders in manufacturing, consumer goods, financial services and technology. Cloudyn was founded in 2012 by (pictured on the left from left to right): Vittaly Tavor (VP Products), Sharon Wagner (CEO) and Dr. Boris Goldberg (CTO)

name: Clarizen
description: Clarizen delivers secure, cloud-based collaborative work management solutions built on the vision of business agility. Clarizen combines cross-company project management with configurable workflow automation to power the agile enterprise. Discussions, tasks, projects and portfolios are all accessible from Clarizen’s scalable enterprise platform. Internal and external stakeholders both gain easy access to a single source of information to improve work execution, collaborate in-context, optimize resources and respond faster. Clarizen is a leader in Forrester’s Enterprise Collaborative Work Management report and is a two-time Leader in Gartner’s Magic Quadrant for Cloud-Based IT Project and Portfolio Management.

name: SnapTu Ltd. / Facebook
description: The app was created by an Israeli startup called Moblica and was originally known as Moblica.[2] Snaptu's focus was its ability to connect users with even a rudimentary phone to the mobile web. The product's cross-platform capabilities stem from its methodology, in which the applications do not run on the mobile phone itself, but on Internet servers. Snaptu was a collection of apps including Twitter, LinkedIn, Picasa, Flickr and others, available from its own app store.[3] Snaptu bundled more than 30 free applications and more than 25 web links as of September 23, 2010.[4][better source needed] In January 2011, the Snaptu application had over 78 million users worldwide. A press release in March 2011 at the company blog confirmed that the company has agreed to be acquired by Facebook.

description: Zend Technologies is a leader in end-to-end PHP web and mobile application development and deployment solutions. With 50 percent of the web workload running on PHP, including Magento, Drupal, and WordPress, Zend products drive PHP in the enterprise, from code creation through production deployment. The company was acquired in 2015 by Rogue Wave Software. https://www.zend.com/

By replacing scarce and expensive materials like cobalt with scalable alternatives, TexPower is helping strengthen domestic battery supply chains and accelerate the transition to cleaner, more affordable electrification.

name: Thea Energy
description: Thea Energy is reimagining how fusion power gets built -- starting with a fundamental rethink of the magnet. Spun out of Princeton University and the Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory, the company is developing a stellarator, a type of fusion device that can run in a continuous, stable state without sudden plasma disruptions that have long plagued its better-known cousin, the tokamak. Traditional stellarators achieve that stability through magnets with elaborate, custom-sculpted three-dimensional shapes. This has historically made stellarators impractical to manufacture and maintain at scale. Thea's key insight is to flip that logic: instead of building complexity into the physical shape of the magnets, they use arrays of simple, flat (planar) coils and let software do the heavy lifting. The result is a fusion system that is not only more stable, but dramatically easier to build, service, and replicate -- a critical ingredient for deploying fusion energy at real-world scale.

name: Traxen
description: Traxen Inc. is a pioneering company at the forefront of innovative solutions in the transportation industry. Committed to revolutionizing the movement of goods, Traxen specializes in the development of cutting-edge technologies that optimize fleet management and enhance overall efficiency. Through a blend of advanced data analytics, artificialintelligence, and a deep understanding of logistics, Traxen strives to create intelligent solutions that not only improve operational performance but also contribute to a more sustainable and connected future in transportation.

name: Type One Energy
description: Type One Energy was born from a dinner conversation at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, where leading stellarator scientists decided to stop waiting for academia and build the next leap in fusion themselves. The founders didn't just study stellarators; they built five of them, including UW-Madison's HSX machine and Germany's Wendelstein 7-X, the world's largest. Their approach preserves the stellarator's defining feature (i.e., physically twisted, non-planar magnets that hold superheated plasma in a stable, continuous flow) but unlocks it with two modern breakthroughs: high-temperature superconducting (HTS) magnets that generate far stronger fields than conventional materials, and advances in supercomputing that enable plasma optimization at previously impossible precision. Together, these clear the barriers that kept stellarators confined to research labs for decades. The company is building Infinity One, an engineering verification platform at TVA's Bull Run Energy Complex in Tennessee, scheduled for 2029, followed by Infinity Two, a 400-megawatt commercial fusion power plant designed to put clean electricity on the grid.

Atana has developed a better, smarter way to find and develop high-value assets quickly and with great precision. description: Caporus’ patented capacitor technologies enable reliable capacitive energy storage and filtering at the higher voltages and temperatures required by the next generation of high density power conversion systems. Caporus dielectrics employ Nanoscale Lamellar Porosity (NLP) to meet the increasingly demanding requirements for power conversion systems that are key to supporting the electrification of transportation and integration of distributed energy resources on the grid. The combination of advanced manufacturing processes and novel materials represents a long-awaited and significant advancement in efficiency and power density in power electronics and power conversion systems and has the potential to reduce the need for rare earth elements in electric motors.

Divi-H can be used in a wide range of applications, from fuel gas recovery to loop optimization through H2/CO adjustment and carbon capture, and can operate in refineries, petrochemical plants, ammonia plants, methanol production, metallurgical production, power-to-gas systems, gasifiers and many other locations.

name: Echion Technologies

XNO® enables batteries to fast charge safely in less than 10 minutes, with high energy density and a cycle life of more than 10,000 cycles.XNO® materials are based on proprietary mixed Niobium oxide compositions and microparticle designs protected by 13 international patent families and are now being scaled-up to the multi-thousand tonne/year production scale. The differentiated technology helps cell manufacturers gain a technical and commercial advantage in high-value, fast-growing markets where end-users require the safety, low total cost of ownership, and unique performance mix offered by XNO®.This includes industrial and commercial e-mobility markets: rail, marine, AGVs, mining trucks and other off-highway vehicles, opportunity-charging e-buses and other high-utilisation EV fleets. XNO® also provides a unique value proposition for the micro-battery market and specific applications for the ESS, motorsports, and medical markets. ‍

name: Energy Vault

At Energy Vault, we work to combat climate change by enabling clean and reliable electricity through innovation in renewable energy storage. Utilizing a unique approach to the circular economy that integrates energy waste for beneficial reuse at unprecedented economics, Energy Vault innovates to accelerate the shift to a fully renewable world.

name: FluoRok
description: FluoRok (Oxford, UK) is reinventing fluorochemicals manufacturing and the way the world accesses fluorinated products such as Li-ion battery electrolyte salts and additives. FluoRok’s proprietary process bypasses for the first time the energy intensive intermediary hydrofluoric acid (HF), one of the most hazardous and difficult-to-handle chemicals on the planet. FluoRok’s solutions are safer, more sustainable, lower cost, and introduce for the first time the circular economy in fluorochemical manufacturing. Spun-out of the University of Oxford, UK in 2022, the team has decades of combined experience in fluorine chemistry and business development and is currently working towards their first pilot plant.

name: Iontra
description: Iontra Inc, a Denver-based battery performance and safety technology company, has been in stealth mode for nearly a decade and is partnered with various OEMs to commercialize its breakthrough charging technology that will replace incumbent CC/CV charging and drastically reduce the development time of new batteries and battery-powered products. Iontra has found a fundamental way to materially reduce degradation in lithium batteries when charging or discharging, opening the door to more than two-fold improvements in charging speed and cycle life, improved capacity utilization, and safe cold-temperature charging.

name: Khemia Metals
description: Khemia Metals is enabling more sustainable batteries by replacing critical metals with earth-abundant alloys. Khemia leverages high-throughput alloy discovery to develop alloys that are mechanically robust, electrically conductive, and electrochemically stable in battery electrolytes. Khemia is commercializinga next-generation alloy current collector to replace copper foil allowing for lighter, cheaper, and greener batteries.

name: Liminal
description: Liminal is accelerating the transition to electric mobility by transforming battery manufacturing with better data and analytics. Their battery manufacturing intelligence solutions leverage ultrasound and machine learning technology to improve battery cost, quality, and reliability.

name: Monolith
description: EXITED INVESTMENT: Monolith has developed a platform solution that leverages AI and machine learning to solve intractable physics and engineering problems in the testing and validation space. The company has identified battery and EV testing as its beachhead market where extended test cycles in the West put companies at a distinct disadvantage compared to their Chinese counterparts. Monolith is already helping a number of tier 1 automotive companies to optimise their battery testing, enabling them to bring products to market faster. After expanding in this beachhead market, Monolith will apply its platform to the testing and validation space in other industry verticals, such as semiconductors.

name: Monomyth Materials (M2)
description: Monomyth Materials (M2) is a Chicago-based advanced materials company controlled by Monomyth Group, a diversified holding company founded by Chip Dunn in 2017. Its subsidiaries include M2Graphite, which is developing America’s first commercial-scale battery-grade synthetic graphite capacity, and M2Innovations, which advances next-generation materials such as silicon anode technologies and SiOx production through its NanoGraf asset acquisition. Together, M2 is the only integrated active anode material producer in the Western Hemisphere, building a compliant dual-use supply chain and U.S. battery lab network.

name: Nanoscale Components
description: Nanoscale Components has developed a novel, cost-effective process to pre-lithiate lithium-ion battery electrodes. This process enables cell manufacturers to use high-specific capacity materials such as silicon to make cells with higher energy density and improve the cycle life of those materials.

name: Natron Energy
description: Natron Energy’s mission is to transform industrial and grid energy storage markets by providing customers with lower cost, longer lasting, more efficient, safer batteries. Natron’s battery products are based on a unique Prussian blue chemistry and can integrate into a wide variety of energy storage applications ranging from critical backup power systems to EV fast charging and behind-the-meter applications. Natron’s batteries are UL1973 recognized and have passed rigorous UL9540A fire testing, offer higher power density, faster recharge and significantly longer cycle life than other energy storage technologies. Natron builds its batteries using commodity materials on existing cell manufacturing lines. Natron is backed by leading venture capital investors including ABB Technology Ventures, Chevron, Khosla Ventures, Nano Dimension, Prelude Ventures and Volta Energy Technologies.

name: Niron Magnetics
description: Niron Magnetics is developing the world’s first advanced manufacturing process for the mass production of permanent magnets powered by its breakthrough material formulation. Niron’s proprietary Iron nitride magnets possess inherently higher magnetization and can be produced at a lower cost compared to today’s rare-earth magnets and will enable a revolution in the design of new electric motors and generators.

name: One Next Energy
description: Our Next Energy Inc. (ONE) is a Michigan-based developer of innovative energy storage solutions with a vision to rapidly expand the world’s access to sustainable power. Founded in 2020 by Mujeeb Ijaz, a battery systems engineer with more than 30 years of experience, ONE and its team of experienced battery engineers are focused on safer battery chemistries that use the most sustainable raw materials while creating a reliable, low cost and conflict-free supply chain.

name: OneD Battery
description: OneD’s SINANODE™ technology platform fuses nano-silicon into commercial graphites – increasing the performance of EV batteries while lowering costs. Silicon nanowires provide 3,250 mA/g of reversible capacity and avoid the expansion and breakage issues of other solutions such as silicon oxide. The result is faster charging, longer range, and affordable EVs.With over 240 patents, OneD Battery Sciences has joint development agreements with many industry partners including GM, which is also an investor.

name: Percepto
description: Percepto’s holistic solution enables fully automated inspections and continuous monitoring of critical infrastructure around the globe. This is all facilitated by a visionary team based in the US and Israel, focused on pushing the boundaries of industrial automation.

name: Pyka
description: Pyka is America’s leading manufacturer of dual-use, heavy-lift autonomous aircraft. Its autonomous electric crop protection aircraft are in daily commercial use by some of the world’s largest agricultural producers, lowering spray costs for growers by increasing efficiency and reducing chemical use. Pyka is extending its commercially proven autonomy stack to hybrid-electric aircraft, advancing a new paradigm for dual-use logistics and defense capabilities. The platform delivers long-range, heavy-lift performance with the flexibility to support multiple missions in environments with limited infrastructure. Pyka’s vertically integrated manufacturing enables scalable, cost-effective production across its products.

name: Resonant Link
description: Resonant Link delivers 5x faster and highly-efficient wireless power for applications big to small, from massive industrial trucks to medical devices smaller than a fingernail. Resonant Link is anchored by offices in South Burlington, VT, Zurich, CH, and Boston, MA, and has amassed double-digit customers in healthcare, electric vehicles, and consumer electronics. With backing from top investors and government agencies, Resonant Link is poised to continue its exponential growth and lead the movement to electrify work, logistics, transportation, and patient care to help people, businesses, and the planet thrive.

name: Solid Power
description: Solid Power is an industry-leading developer of all solid-state rechargeable batteries for electric vehicles and mobile power markets. Founded in 2012 as a spin-out from the University of Colorado Boulder, Solid Power replaces the flammable liquid electrolyte in a conventional lithium-ion battery with a proprietary sulfide solid electrolyte. As a result, Solid Power’s all solid-state batteries are safer and more stable across a broad temperature range, can provide a 50-100% increase in energy density compared to the best available rechargeable batteries, enable cheaper, more energy-dense battery pack designs and are compatible with traditional lithium-ion manufacturing processes. Solid Power has extensive partnerships with both BMW and Ford to jointly develop all solid-state batteries using the company’s Louisville-based megawatt-hour-scale (MWh) production line. In addition to Volta, Solid Power is backed by prominent investors including Samsung, Hyundai, Ford, and Solvay.

name: ANAPHITE
description: Anaphite offers an industry-leading solution to the challenges of dry coating cathodes with its chemical compositing process to make dry coating precursor powders. The patented technology has the potential to make EV battery manufacturing 30% less carbon intensive and 40% cheaper, and the UK-based company is already working with global car and battery cell manufacturers. Anaphite has patented chemistry-based battery electrode production technology that reduces the cost of EV batteries by 5-10% - independent of the battery chemistry. The company has already proven the technology’s capability in lithium-ion battery production, and it will also be applicable to a wide range of new battery technologies, including sodium-ion and solid state. The team’s exceptionally pragmatic and future-focused mindset is another key asset. Alex and Sam brought in Joe Stevenson as CEO in 2022 when they were looking to scale and reach customers. Joe is an experienced commercial lead at the helm of the company, and has helped Anaphite progress to the next level. This type of foresight is absolutely essential when creating new technology companies, where’s the next gap and how to fill it, and puts them in the best position to scale quickly. The scale of Anaphite’s ambition and potential is also clearly reflected in the consortium of the Series A. We’re experienced investors based all around the world, from our round co-leads Maniv in the US/Israel, to EEI in Japan, and Nesta in the UK. We all believe this company has what it takes to win across geographies. This company is setting new standards for battery production and can help us reach a decarbonised future faster and more efficiently. We're looking forward to helping Anaphite’s technology go global and reduce the costs of the entire battery industry to the benefit of all. name: Barocal
description: Barocal is replacing harmful refrigerants with high-efficiency solid-state cooling technology for the $500B global HVAC market. Cambridge-based Barocal is commercialising solid-state cooling using barocaloric materials, a breakthrough resulting from 15 years of research at the University of Cambridge. Instead of cycling high-GWP refrigerant gases like conventional systems, Barocal’s technology applies pressure to proprietary solid-state barocaloric materials to transfer heat. This eliminates refrigerant leakage and the emissions associated with it. Why we invested in Barocal The climate case : Cooling emits over 4 Gt CO₂e annually, accounting for more than 7% of global greenhouse gas emissions, which makes it one of the largest decarbonisation blind spots. These emissions come from HFC refrigerant leakage, which often have global warming potentials more than 1,000 times higher than CO₂, as well as from the energy intensity of cooling itself. Cooling demand is projected to triple by 2050 , further increasing these emissions. Barocal directly addresses both leakage and energy consumption by eliminating refrigerant gases entirely and delivering significantly higher efficiency than existing solutions. The business case : The global HVAC market is worth approximately $450 billion and is expected to grow to $577 billion by 2033. Barocal is initially focused on commercial chillers and data centre cooling, targeting some of the fastest-growing and most profitable segments. The company is working in collaboration with large OEMs to bring the technology to market. In addition to the emissions benefits, higher efficiency reduces energy costs and results in a lower total cost of ownership for customers. The team : Prof. Xavier Moya, Co-Founder and CEO, is a Professor of Materials Physics at the University of Cambridge and a globally recognised pioneer in caloric materials and barocalorics. He has authored more than 150 scientific publications with over 15,000 citations. He founded Barocal to commercialise his breakthrough research, funded by the Royal Society and the European Research Council. Dr. Giles Rodway, Co-Founder and CTO, brings decades of industrial R&D experience from the automotive sector and previously founded Spinetic, combining deep engineering expertise with proven entrepreneurial credibility. Website: https://barocal.com/ Founded 2019 Management Prof. Xavier Moya Dr. Giles Rodway Location Cambridge, UK Segment Industry World Fund Investment Stage

name: Enerkii
description: enerkii is slashing industrial energy bills while decarbonising one of Europe’s hardest-to-abate sectors. The Munich-based company provides a full-service, emissions-free energy system for industrial and commercial players across Europe. By combining software intelligence with on-site renewable infrastructure, enerkii enables companies to cut their energy bills by up to 50%, with zero upfront investment. Through its unique “Energy-as-a-Service” model, enerkii is eliminating the complexity, risk, and cost of industrial decarbonisation. Why we invested in enerkii The climate case: Energy production accounts for ~75% of global CO₂ emissions, and industrial energy use remains one of the slowest sectors to decarbonise. Over 80% of industrial sites in Germany still rely on fossil fuels despite increasing renewable availability. enerkii directly addresses this by enabling affordable, zero-emission on-site energy generation. With 87 MW of contracted capacity already secured, enerkii is on track to reduce industrial emissions at scale - just as Germany and the EU accelerate towards 2030 renewable energy targets. The business case: enerkii unlocks an enormous untapped market: the decarbonisation of Europe’s commercial and industrial sectors. While competitors focus on point solutions, enerkii offers a fully integrated system, including solar, battery storage, charging infrastructure, and (soon) heat pumps. These assets are backed by a proprietary Operating System (OS) that configures optimal setups in minutes. Their business model is elegant and compelling: no investment, no complexity, just savings. enerkii already has 18 contracts with major German industrial players, and is well-positioned for Europe-wide expansion. The team: Co-founder and CEO David Balensiefen is a serial entrepreneur who previously co-founded gridX, which he successfully exited to E.ON. He is joined by gridX veterans Henry Thierhoff and Hendrik Abel, forming a team with deep technical knowledge, proven operational execution, and a bold vision for building Europe’s next major decentralised energy provider. name: FARMLESS
description: FARMLESS CREATES CARBON NEGATIVE, FUNCTIONAL PROTEINS THAT CUT OUT THE NEED FOR AGRICULTURAL LAND. The Farmless process combines the ancient craft of fermentation – which has been used for millennia to brew beer and bake bread – with a modern feedstock, the scientific term for a starter liquid. Why we invested: The climate case: Whereas most fermentation companies rely on sugar, Farmless uses a feedstock made from CO2, water, nitrogen and renewable energy – bypassing the need for agricultural land. Agriculture has taken over almost half of all habitable land on earth, pushing nature over the brink, and the world needs an affordable protein source that can be produced without excessive land use. The business case: the demand for meat and dairy is set to soar with a growing population, and we need dramatically more efficient, scalable ways of protein production - fast. Farmless’ technology will help scale alternative proteins which meet long-term, buoyant consumer demand. The team: the Farmless team, led by Adnan Oner, combines physicists, food experts, communications leaders and data analysts who will drive the start-up forward in the coming years. name: Hyperscale Power
description: HYPERSCALE POWER IS BUILDING THE NEXT GENERATION OF ELECTRIC POWER INFRASTRUCTURE. The Zurich-based deeptech company is developing compact solid-state transformers (SSTs) designed for the power demands of AI data centres, EV charging, and large-scale renewable energy systems. Hyperscale Power’s proprietary design is roughly 10× smaller than conventional transformers and uses around 90% less material, dramatically reducing deployment timelines from years to weeks. By leveraging high-frequency operation and advanced power electronics, the system achieves energy-conversion efficiencies of up to 98.5% – significantly higher than today’s solutions. With a clear efficiency, cost, and emissions advantage, Hyperscale Power is positioned to unlock faster electrification and power delivery for the infrastructure underpinning the next industrial era. Why we invested in Hyperscale Power The climate case: Electricity systems lose around 6–8% of generated power globally through transmission and conversion inefficiencies. At the same time, the rapid growth of AI compute, EV charging networks, and renewable power generation is dramatically increasing electricity demand. Hyperscale Power’s solid-state transformers offer up to 98.5% energy-conversion efficiency and enable more flexible, modular grid architectures that can integrate renewables more effectively. Even a 2% improvement in efficiency at hyperscale data-centre and grid level translates into millions of tonnes of avoided CO₂ emissions. The company’s compact design also reduces material usage by roughly 90%, lowering embodied emissions and supporting a more resource-efficient power infrastructure. The business case: Hyperscale Power is entering a rapidly expanding multi-billion-euro market driven by hyperscalers, electrification, and global investment in energy infrastructure. Transformer supply chains are currently strained, with lead times stretching to 18–24 months as demand for high-power systems accelerates. Hyperscale Power’s SST technology dramatically shortens deployment timelines while delivering higher efficiency and power density. This creates a compelling value proposition for data centres, EV charging networks, and renewable-energy operators that need faster, more efficient power conversion to meet growing electricity demands. The team: Hyperscale Power was founded in 2025 by Daniel Rothmund and Sami Pettersson, who each bring more than a decade of experience in solid-state transformers and medium-voltage high-power converters. Their deep technical expertise in power electronics and transformer architecture underpins the company’s proprietary design. Based in Zurich, the team benefits from close ties to Europe’s leading engineering ecosystem around ETH Zürich, positioning the company to attract top technical talent and rapidly bring its technology to market. Website: Hyperscale Power Founded 2025 Management Daniel Rothmund, CEO Sami Pettersson, CTO Location Zürich, Switzerland Segment Energy World Fund Investment Stage
